data.title: Configuration File
data.tagline: A structured file containing runtime settings and environment parameters for software to parse upon startup or runtime.
data.learningOutcome: You can distinguish the config's platform and model choice from the way the model should work under project rules.
data.description: For example, an AI tool may read its model, endpoint, timeout, and permission settings from a config file, while project rules describe the stack and collaboration conventions for the current codebase. A config may reference secret variable names, but real secrets belong in environment variables or a secret manager and must not be tracked by git.

learning.assumes: You know that an AI tool needs a model service.
learning.outcome: You can distinguish the config's platform and model choice from the way the model should work under project rules.

distinctions.label: Project Rules
distinctions.explanation: A Configuration File configures the tool's runtime settings (such as model, Base URL, or timeout); Project Rules instruct the AI on coding conventions and project constraints.

explanation.title: Config files store runtime settings (JSON / YAML / TOML)
explanation.text: Stores provider, model, endpoint, port, or permission parameters. Common formats include JSON (strict key-value), YAML (supports comments), and TOML (clear sections).

explanation.title: Project rules specify collaboration requirements
explanation.text: Project rules describe the constraints and conventions the model must follow in the current codebase, such as stack, code style, and boundaries.

explanation.title: Restart usually required after changes
explanation.text: Most tools only read configs on startup. Modifying next.config.js, .env, or tailwind.config.ts usually requires restarting the dev server (Ctrl+C then npm run dev).

lessonPractice.title: What type of file should you check first when a model call fails?

options.label: The config file
options.feedback: Correct. First check the Provider, model, and connection settings in the config file.

options.label: The project rules file
options.feedback: Not quite. First check the Provider, model, and connection settings in the config file.

options.label: The page style file
options.feedback: Not quite. First check the Provider, model, and connection settings in the config file.

data.agentPrompt: First identify which config file this tool actually loads, then check its model, endpoint, and timeout settings. Do not read or print real secrets; report the effective path and configuration layer.
